correctness.rationale: Finite superlevel sets give the rank-truncation upper bound; finite disjoint bump functions give a factorization of the identity through the multiplier for the universal strict-s-number lower bound. Infinite superlevel sets give an isometric c0 obstruction to strict singularity, while finite truncations give the matching compact-distance upper bound.

originality.rationale: Discrete diagonal approximation formulas and abstract essential-norm results are prior art and are excluded from the novelty claim. No inspected source gave the simultaneous all-strict-s-number C0 formula together with the exact compact/FSS/SS distance collapse. Aksoy--Lewicki (1997) and older diagonal/central-operator literature remain explicit residual risks.

value.rationale: A single topological order statistic determines every finite strict s-number and all three principal compactness/strict-singularity distances, with explicit 1-complemented finite witnesses and a flat-profile corollary on perfect compact spaces.
